sources.title: Cloud-native resampling and reprojection in Python — Development Seed
sources.date: Results page processes results/2024-11-01; source repository inspected at a611e4fea1027f460625cea5c67760b9d10573cc (2026-04-03). These dates describe different artifacts.

benchmark_setup.data: One timestep and variable from real MUR SST and GPM IMERG; full resolution input, Web Mercator 256×256 output tiles at multiple zoom extents. MUR SST input is 0.01-degree global.
benchmark_setup.methods: Initial comparison uses nearest neighbour, including Rasterio, rioxarray, odc-geo, Pyresample and xESMF with/without pre-generated weights. Local/cloud NetCDF, virtualized Zarr, converted Zarr and overview-enabled formats.
benchmark_setup.hardware: JupyterHub/Docker environment documented; exact CPU model/count, RAM and thread settings not found in inspected summary and runner source.
benchmark_setup.timing: utils.process_results takes pyinstrument_data["duration"] from a fresh profiled script. Script includes imports, file opening/read/crop and completed load/compute. Weight-free and cached xESMF are separate variants. Not matched to our import-excluded timing.
benchmark_setup.accuracy: Not a numerical-accuracy or conservation benchmark; no RMSE-based ranking is supplied.

evidence.excerpt: ODC and Rioxarray (both based on GDAL) consistently had relatively fast times and low memory usage.
Rasterio had similar memory usage and time for local tile generation to ODC and Rioxarray, but was much slower for remote files.
XESMF without pre-generated weights was consistently the slowest method.

MUR SST zoom 0 saved table: rasterio / COG / local duration 0.451393 s; rioxarray / NetCDF / h5netcdf / local 24.109180 s; odc / NetCDF / h5netcdf / local 29.754768 s. These rows differ in storage/overview configuration and are not a pure library comparison.
da.load() precedes return xr_reproject(da, gbox).load(); this ODC example materializes cropped input before reprojection.

comparison.relationship: Directional agreement with major scope differences
comparison.our_evidence: Our rectilinear 1024 xESMF bilinear means: 37.990 s setup + 0.447 s application. Our Web Mercator 4096 total means: Rasterio 1.23 s, rioxarray 1.39 s, odc-geo 1.88 s, essentially identical smooth-field RMSE/coverage.
comparison.interpretation: Supports separating xESMF weight construction from reuse and treating GDAL raster wrappers as competitive local reprojection workflows. It also limits our preference: the external remote-file result reverses a simplistic Rasterio-is-always-fastest conclusion because readers and access patterns matter. Our in-memory kernels and warm NetCDF control cannot establish cloud tile-serving performance.
comparison.recommendation_effect: Keep Rasterio/rioxarray local-raster preference conditional; add explicit reader/overview/network caveat and cache weight advice.

limitations: No direct throughput or speedup ratio against our runs: different hardware, real input dimensions, 256² tile outputs, nearest rather than our bilinear CRS kernels, process/import/I/O boundaries and data locality.
Published summary warns that xESMF may be appropriate for conservation/curvilinear workloads despite slow setup; its nearest tile benchmark does not adjudicate conservative accuracy.
The ODC example is not proof of fully lazy out-of-core input execution; it calls load() before warp.

sources.title: GeoUtils scaling benchmarks — reprojection by raster size
sources.type: published benchmark dashboard / machine-readable ASV-derived measurements
sources.date: Raw JSON metadata date 2026-09-19T21:32:05Z; commit a31a03838b63bb9e39d21d0d956c72f1bcad2282. Dashboard summary and raw JSON can refer to different revisions; values below are from raw JSON.

benchmark_setup.data: WGS84 EPSG:4326 raster → UTM32N EPSG:32632, nearest neighbour, preserving selected output dimensions. Raster side lengths 1024,2048,4096.
benchmark_setup.methods: GeoUtils Rasterio/GDAL calculation engine under eager, Dask and multiprocessing execution; standalone GDAL CLI also supplied. Summary reference workload uses 512×512 chunks.
benchmark_setup.hardware: Machine github-actions-x64-f56edd1d, Python /home/runner/miniconda3/envs/geoutils-dev/bin/python. Published dashboard states one computational process and one thread; detailed CPU model not in downloaded metadata.
benchmark_setup.timing: Raw JSON distinguishes operation_time_s (after execution-mode initialization) from end_to_end_time_s (prepared inputs through completed output). The latter includes worker/CLI startup.
benchmark_setup.accuracy: Timing and memory dashboard; no common-footprint RMSE or conservation evidence in these records.

evidence.excerpt: All options run without parallelism: one computational process using one thread.
Reprojects a WGS84 (EPSG:4326) raster to UTM zone 32N (EPSG:32632) with nearest-neighbor resampling while preserving the selected output dimensions.

reprojection-raster-size, parameter 2048: eager operation_time_s 1.0428038770000967, end_to_end_time_s 1.049540535000233; Dask operation_time_s 1.888733711499981, end_to_end_time_s 3.6690352219998204.
reprojection-raster-size, parameter 4096: eager operation_time_s 4.118796545499663, end_to_end_time_s 4.134179817000586; Dask operation_time_s 8.59900268899969, end_to_end_time_s 10.462309581999762.

comparison.relationship: Agreement that lazy/chunked execution has nontrivial overhead in serial runs
comparison.our_evidence: Our synchronous single-thread chunk suite keeps geometry fixed: xarray rectilinear compute medians 0.508/0.094/0.039 s for (1,128,128)/(1,256,256)/(4,512,512). odc-geo Web Mercator 0.239/0.129/0.085 s; graph task counts128/32/2.
comparison.interpretation: The external eager/Dask gap supports our warning that chunking is an execution strategy rather than an automatic speed gain. Its separate operation/end-to-end measurements also reinforce exposing execution initialization costs. It does not validate our exact optimal chunk size or our odc-geo accuracy discrepancy.
comparison.recommendation_effect: Continue to require measured compute rather than graph construction alone, and use eager/full chunks when data fits and latency dominates.

limitations: Different wrapper, nearest kernel, UTM destination, and dataset geometry; no cross-site seconds or package speedups are comparable.
Dask is intentionally single-worker, so this cannot establish multiworker or distributed scaling.
No claim that lower eager time is preferable when dataset exceeds available memory.
No external accuracy evidence for our four finite-mask differences in one odc-geo LV95 layout.

sources.title: SERTIT Open Source Rasters Comparison — use case reprojection benchmark
sources.type: exploratory benchmark notebook with saved outputs; methodological caveats
sources.date: Repository inspected at 30575de1f0c2e6241f87cfebecb52659ea7be21d (2026-07-21); execution date not recorded in inspected notebook.

benchmark_setup.data: Real Pléiades Neo image subsets: one band, 9104×5758 (~100MB),29135×18426 (~1GB),71367×45135 (~6GB). Target EPSG4326; notebook says source EPSG:324643, which appears suspect and is not independently resolved.
benchmark_setup.methods: Bilinear Rasterio file-to-file, rioxarray open/reproject/to_raster, and Dask-backed opening followed by rio.reproject/to_raster with varying input chunks.
benchmark_setup.hardware: Intel Core i7-12700K @3.6GHz,64GB RAM,Windows11. Thread and scheduler details not explicitly controlled in inspected timing cells.
benchmark_setup.timing: perf_counter encloses memory_profiler.memory_usage invocation of full file open → default target transform → reprojection → raster write. Profiling overhead/I/O included; no separate setup/application timing, systematic repeat distribution or warm/cold cache control.
benchmark_setup.accuracy: No numerical reference-error or finite-mask comparison in saved timing cells.

evidence.excerpt: The resampling method used for all reprojection scenarios is bilinear.
Saved outputs: Rasterio durations 6.74,30.18,175.71 seconds; rioxarray durations 6.2,25.24,162.83 seconds, for 100MB,1GB,6GB respectively.
At 1GB, Dask-opening chunk1024 duration31.32s and chunk2048 duration25.45s; at6GB chunk2048 164.25s,chunk4096 164.14s,auto166.14s.
The written conclusion says Rasterio: Fastest for simple reprojections; this conflicts with its own saved rioxarray timings.

comparison.relationship: Mixed/contrary ordering; useful only with explicit critique
comparison.our_evidence: Our4096LV95 rioxarray total mean2.05s versus Rasterio2.16s; WebMercator Rasterio1.23s versus rioxarray1.39s.
comparison.interpretation: Its saved outputs reinforce that Rasterio/rioxarray ordering depends on the workload and wrappers; do not repeat the notebook claim that Rasterio always wins. Its chunk-input timings do not prove lazy warp execution: rio.reproject can materialize .values. Versioned primary source below supports this caveat.
comparison.recommendation_effect: Keep both Rasterio/rioxarray as conditional preferences rather than one universal winner; require checking output array type before describing a Dask-backed call as lazy.

limitations: Exploratory single-notebook measurements, no fixed canonical target shape/hash across adapters is demonstrated.
The companion03_reprojection notebook claims rio.reproject creates a lazy Dask graph, which conflicts with verified rioxarray0.19 implementation and docs. Dask on opening does not prove Dask warp.
Source-CRS identifier appears suspect; notebook conclusions contain a timing-order inconsistency. Treat it as lower-confidence evidence, not a validation of our recommendations.

sources.title: rioxarray0.19.0 reproject implementation and Dask note

evidence.excerpt: To re-project with dask, see odc-geo & pyresample.

comparison.relationship: Implementation support for our execution-model caveat
comparison.our_evidence: Our large rioxarray adapter is timed eagerly; chunk suite uses odc-geo for tiled lazy reprojection rather than assuming rio.reproject preserves laziness.
comparison.interpretation: Corroborates checking actual execution/output chunks instead of treating Dask-backed input as proof of lazy output. Also supplies a primary-source correction to SERTIT companion notebook narration.
comparison.recommendation_effect: Retain existing separation between eager rioxarray and tested lazy odc-geo; do not infer behavior of newer versions without inspection.

limitations: Not an independent speed benchmark; no performance ratio or error ranking follows from source code alone.
